items.title: How failed calls trigger huge economic losses
items.summary: *SMEs lament: Our livelihood goes with poor network connections •Nigeria recorded over 5,000 fibre-optic cuts in six months – NCC •Telcos blame fiber cuts, vandalism, power By Juliet Umeh For Nigeria’s growing army of internet-reliant entrepreneurs and workers, the network bars on a mobile phone can mean the difference between earning a living and going […] The post How failed calls trigger huge e
items.body: *SMEs lament: Our livelihood goes with poor network connections •Nigeria recorded over 5,000 fibre-optic cuts in six months – NCC •Telcos blame fiber cuts, vandalism, power By Juliet Umeh For Nigeria’s growing army of internet-reliant entrepreneurs and workers, the network bars on a mobile phone can mean the difference between earning a living and going home empty-handed. For an online seller, a lost connection can mean a missed order; for a ride-hailing driver, a missed trip; for a POS operator, a failed transaction; and for an online tutor, a disrupted class. Increasingly, the internet is no longer just a tool for communication. For millions of workers and small businesses, it has become the marketplace, payment channel, classroom, dispatch system and customer-service desk. But when the connection disappears, so does the livelihood built around it. For Mrs Anna Nso, a small business centre owner in Aba, Abia State, a poor network has become a daily battle with frustrated customers, financial losses and mounting anxiety. One day, a network glitch turned a routine electricity payment into a costly mistake. “My husband wanted to recharge N1,900 electricity bill for a customer, but because of the network problem, he mistakenly recharged N19,000,” Nso told Vanguard. “The network stressed him so much that he made the mistake.” It was not an isolated incident. “There are times we transfer money twice because we don’t know the first transfer has gone through. If you don’t check the transaction history before trying again, you can end up making a double transfer,” she said. The pressure is compounded when customers crowd her shop waiting for transactions to go through. “You discover that customers will line up in the shop, waiting for me to attend to them. In the process, I will be turning my phone up and down, moving from one corner to another in search of a network,” she said. The stress has also begun to take a toll. “I recently checked my BP because I was having constant headaches and feeling dizzy. My nurse told me it was 150 over 100. Honestly, I wasn’t surprised. The challenge I face in my shop every day is enough to give someone a headache,” she said. ‘If I’m unreachable, I can’t earn’ For e-hailing driver Polycarp Dawalere, poor network can mean the difference between receiving an order and going home empty-handed. The Taraba State indigene, who formerly lived in Ikorodu, Lagos, said unstable connectivity had become a familiar frustration. “We do have problems with the network, especially in some places in Ikorodu. The network is always very poor in so many areas,” he said. Dawalere depends on digital platforms for his livelihood. “If I am in a place where the network is bad, I can’t get any order because I will be unreachable,” he said. The problem became so serious that it influenced where he lived. “This was the major reason I left Ikorodu. I noticed I was losing clients,” he said. For him, the equation is simple: “If I am unreachable, I cannot get an order. And if I cannot get an order, I cannot earn.” ‘A one-hour class can stretch to 90 minutes’ For Debbie Ntigeli, an online tutor in Ajah, Lagos, unstable connectivity can turn a one-hour lesson into a 90-minute struggle. “With how unstable some of the network providers have been lately, I sometimes experience network delays and disconnections, which interrupt the flow of the lesson,” she said. “It also affects my ability to share learning materials and use interactive tools with my learners.” Sometimes she has to move around her environment searching for a stronger signal. “A class that is supposed to last for one hour can sometimes extend to an hour and 30 minutes because of time lost to network interruptions,” she said. The cost of staying connected also comes directly from her pocket. “I spend about N25,000 monthly on data. Data is one of my major teaching-related expenses,” she said. For Ntigeli, connectivity is therefore not an optional expenditure. It is part of the cost of earning an income. When the shop lives on a phone For Lagos fashion entrepreneur Tomiwa Ibukunle, the vulnerability of an online business became clear during the global WhatsApp, Facebook and Instagram outage in October 2021. On an ordinary day, WhatsApp Business brought her about 20 orders. But when the platforms went down, she received only five. For an entrepreneur whose shop largely exists on a smartphone screen, the lesson was painful: When connectivity disappears, the shop can disappear with it. Another fashion seller, Dolapo, initially thought her own network was responsible when messages and calls stopped working. Then she realised: “WhatsApp was down.” For her, the platform was her enquiry desk, order channel and customer-service platform. A similar experience confronted Lagos fashion vendor Adaeze Nathan during an Instagram outage in 2026. When messages stopped sending, she discovered that the problem was not her internet connection but the platform itself. The experiences expose a new vulnerability for Nigeria’s small businesses. For entrepreneurs whose storefronts, customer relationships and payment channels exist largely online, connectivity is no longer a convenience. It is infrastructure. The infrastructure behind the disappearing bars Behind these individual experiences is a larger infrastructure challenge. The Nigerian Communications Commission, NCC, disclosed that more than 5,000 fibre-optic cut incidents were recorded in the first six months of 2026, largely linked to road construction, excavation and other civil works. NCC Executive Vice Chairman, Dr Aminu Maida, warned that the damage goes beyond the cables. “To a machine operator on a construction site, it may appear to be a simple buried cable. To the nation, it can mean failed calls, delayed payments, interrupted services and missed opportunities,” Maida said. He stressed that Nigeria must build roads while protecting the fibre networks that connect the economy. The scale of Nigeria’s digital dependence is reflected in data consumption. NCC figures show that Nigerians consumed more than 1.5 million terabytes of data in May 2026, rising to about 1.53 million TB in June. Industry raises alarm The telecom industry says the problem is compounded by vandalism, inadequate infrastructure and other operational challenges. The Association of Licensed Telecom Operators of Nigeria, ALTON, said network sabotage and vandalism, including stolen fibre cables and base-station equipment, continue to degrade connectivity. Its Chairman, Engr Gbenga Adebayo, said such incidents affect millions of subscribers. The Association of Telecommunications Companies of Nigeria, ATCON, also identified inadequate last-mile connectivity and limited fibre penetration as challenges, particularly in underserved areas. MTN Nigeria said it experiences between 35 and 40 fibre cuts daily across the country, arising from road construction, vandalism, sabotage and other factors. The company also disclosed that an average of one to two telecom sites are vandalised every day, with generators, batteries, solar equipment and other critical infrastructure stolen or damaged. In 2025 alone, MTN recorded 452 incidents of site vandalism, according to its General Manager, Network Services, Asura Mshelia. He warned that repeated attacks could make further investment in affected locations difficult to justify. Power: the other side Even where fibre infrastructure remains intact, electricity remains a threat to network reliability. Airtel Africa Chief Executive Officer, Sunil Taldar, said inadequate power supply was one of the biggest challenges facing telecom operators in Nigeria. “To compensate for non-availability of power, what do mobile operators do? We run most of our sites through diesel,” he said. “So, what we’re doing is we are delivering a network, but we are also becoming power generators. Now, that’s not our core job.” Taldar said diesel-powered sites cost almost four times more to operate than those running on grid electricity. He also warned that when telecom networks go down, the impact extends beyond telecommunications. “Each time when a telecom network comes down, it’s not only the telecom network which is coming down in a particular area, it’s part of the economy which is coming down,” he said. For Nso, however, the issue is far simpler than fibre routes, vandalism, power supply or broadband targets. What matters to her are the customers waiting in her shop, the transactions that need to be completed and the money that needs to be transferred. Whenever the signal disappears, she moves from one corner of her shop to another, raises her phone and waits, hoping to find a stronger connection. Sometimes the transaction goes through, sometimes it fails, and at other times she is left wondering whether making another attempt could create a second problem. items.title: Obi Blocked In Benue – A Warning Sign For The 2027 Campaign?
items.summary: The incident could reflect political hostility, a breakdown in local coordination, a security failure, or another cause. The post Obi Blocked In Benue – A Warning Sign For The 2027 Campaign? appeared first on Channels Television .
items.body: THE SIGNAL Peter Obi’s convoy was blocked by youths in Benue State on Tuesday while he was travelling along the Gboko, Makurdi road towards Yelwata, where he was expected to visit communities and families affected by recent violence. The police confirmed the obstruction and said security personnel were providing protection to the former Anambra State governor. The reason for the blockade, however, remained unclear. That distinction matters. Obi said youths, allegedly mobilised by a Special Assistant to the Benue State Government, were responsible. The Benue State Government denied any involvement and said it was not aware of the visit. So far, the incident establishes an obstruction. It does not establish who organised it or why. And that is precisely where the political significance begins. Videos circulating from the scene showed youths blocking the road as Obi’s convoy attempted to pass. Reports indicated chanting and confrontation around the convoy. The police confirmed that the convoy was stopped and said an investigation was underway. Obi described the visit as humanitarian rather than a campaign event, saying he was travelling to express condolences to communities affected by deadly attacks. Other opposition figures, including Rabiu Kwankwaso and Omoyele Sowore, condemned the obstruction. The Benue State Government, however, rejected suggestions that it organised the incident, saying it did not patronise thugs and expected proper coordination with security agencies over political visits. WHAT REMAINS UNRESOLVED Three questions remain central. Who mobilised the youths? Obi has made an allegation. The state government has denied it. That claim and denial cannot, by itself, establish responsibility. Why was the convoy blocked? The incident could reflect political hostility, a breakdown in local coordination, a security failure, or another cause. The available evidence does not yet allow a definitive conclusion. Could it happen again? That may ultimately be the more important question for the 2027 campaign. Nigeria is moving towards a much more intense political season. Candidates will increasingly travel into states and communities where political loyalties are contested and emotions are high. How those movements are managed will matter. WHY THIS MATTERS Elections are not only about who wins votes. They are also about whether candidates can compete for those votes under reasonably equal conditions. A candidate must be able to enter communities, meet voters and present a political argument without being physically obstructed. That does not mean every political visit will be welcomed. Protest, criticism and disagreement are part of democratic politics. But there is a significant difference between rejecting a candidate politically and preventing a candidate from reaching voters. The distinction becomes even more important when security arrangements fail to prevent a confrontation. THE WIDER OPPOSITION SIGNAL The incident comes as opposition politics is simultaneously showing signs of movement and uncertainty. On Monday, Obi appeared publicly with Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde at the inauguration of Makinde’s APM presidential campaign office, where they unveiled a “Reset Nigeria” agenda. Obi has also indicated a willingness to work with any candidate who emerges through a free and fair process. That suggests that, despite continuing disagreements over who should lead an eventual opposition arrangement, engagement between key figures is continuing. The contradiction is notable: the opposition is still trying to create political space for cooperation at the national level, while individual politicians are already encountering the realities of campaigning on the ground. The immediate issue is not political speculation but the outcome of the police investigation. Watch for: •Whether anyone is identified as having organised the blockade. •Whether any arrests or charges follow. •Whether the Benue Government provides further evidence concerning its lack of involvement. •Whether Obi or other opposition candidates alter their campaign plans in response. •Whether similar incidents occur elsewhere as political activity intensifies. One incident does not establish a national pattern. But repeated incidents would begin to establish one. The evidence is incomplete. The standard is not: every candidate must be free to campaign safely and without obstruction. That is today’s Political Signal. Political Signals is an independent political analysis produced for Channels Television. It examines political developments, personalities and electoral trends without endorsement of any political party or candidate. Its assessments are based on publicly available evidence and may change as events and evidence develop. items.title: FG Sets Roadmap For Nationwide Rollout Of 112 Emergency Number
items.summary: The NEC had recently approved 112 as Nigeria’s single universal toll-free emergency number to replace fragmented and slow-response lines, with the aim of eliminating bureaucratic bottlenecks and giving citizens easier access to emergency assistance during fires, accidents, medical crises and security incidents. The post FG Sets Roadmap For Nationwide Rollout Of 112 Emergency Number appeared first
items.body: The Federal Government has directed relevant stakeholders and agencies to develop a comprehensive operational roadmap for the nationwide rollout of the 112 national emergency number. To this end, it has constituted a committee comprising the Nigeria Police Force (NPF), Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC), National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA), Federal Road Safety Corps (FRSC) and other relevant agencies to finalise the roadmap and standard operating procedures for formal endorsement by the National Economic Council (NEC). This was disclosed in a statement issued on Tuesday by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Communications, Office of the Vice President, Stanley Nkwocha. The NEC had recently approved 112 as Nigeria’s single universal toll-free emergency number to replace fragmented and slow-response lines, with the aim of eliminating bureaucratic bottlenecks and giving citizens easier access to emergency assistance during fires, accidents, medical crises and security incidents. Speaking in Abuja on Tuesday at the National Emergency Number 112 Project stakeholders’ meeting, Vice President Kashim Shettima directed the committee to ensure that its decisions and proposed framework were guided by global best practices. Shettima charged the committee to finalise the roadmap and standard operating procedures for formal endorsement by the NEC, stressing the need for the process to make significant progress. He also assured the stakeholders that resources would be made available to drive the implementation once the project becomes more visible. “Let’s make progress so that whatever time we have spent here is worth spending. And most importantly, the engine is finance. It is resources to drive the process. And I want to assure you that we will get the resources,” the Vice President was quoted as saying. The Inspector General of Police, Olatunji Rilwan Disu, expressed the Nigeria Police Force’s full support for the adoption of 112 as the country’s unified national emergency number. From an operational perspective, Disu described the initiative as “a significant step towards ensuring that citizens have a simple and reliable means of accessing emergency assistance.” He explained that citizens facing armed attacks, accidents, fire outbreaks, medical emergencies, kidnapping or other life-threatening situations often first have to determine which agency to contact, stressing that a single number should provide access to the appropriate response agency. Earlier, the Personal Assistant to the President on e-Governance, Office of the Vice President, Lydia Aina, said emergency response in Nigeria currently cuts across several agencies, systems and jurisdictions, resulting in fragmentation in how emergencies are received, coordinated and handled. She said the objective was to move from fragmented state-level systems to a coordinated response mechanism and ultimately establish a fully integrated national framework. According to her, the stakeholders’ meeting focused on the infrastructure and operational framework required to make the emergency number functional, including “the people, the agencies, the standards that make the number actually work when citizens dial it.” “Our job now is to turn it into an actual working programme with milestones. So, we have identified six immediate priorities. First, governance. We need a clear structure of who’s responsible for what,” she explained. Other stakeholders who pledged the full support of their agencies included the Director-General of NEMA, Zubaida Umar; Corps Marshal of the FRSC, Shehu Mohammed; and Director-General of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Lanre Issa-Onilu, among others. items.title: Troops rescue 12 civilians from terrorists in Zamfara

The operations were carried out on Monday, according to the Media Information Officer of Operation Fansan Yamma, Lieutenant Colonel Aliyu Danja. Danja said troops first responded to a distress call after […] Troops rescue 12 civ
items.body: Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have rescued 12 civilians during separate operations against terrorists in Kaura Namoda and Tsafe Local Government Areas of Zamfara State. The operations were carried out on Monday, according to the Media Information Officer of Operation Fansan Yamma, Lieutenant Colonel Aliyu Danja. Danja said troops first responded to a distress call after terrorists invaded a residence at Tsohon Tasha in Kaura Namoda Local Government Area. He said the troops engaged the terrorists, forcing them to abandon six abducted civilians and escape across a nearby river. “The six victims were rescued and later taken to safety before being reunited with their families,” the statement said. In a separate operation in Tsafe Local Government Area, troops monitoring activities along the Main Supply Route spotted terrorists attempting to intercept a Sharon vehicle at Kwanoni Village. According to Danja, the troops quickly moved to the area and engaged the terrorists. “The terrorists were forced to abandon the attack and flee into a nearby bush, allowing the troops to rescue six more civilians,” the statement added. “The two operations demonstrated the commitment of Operation Fansan Yamma to protecting lives and property while disrupting terrorist activities in its area of operation,” it added. Troops rescue 12 civilians from terrorists in Zamfara

items.title: Peter Obi urges FG to end killings, return IDPs to their homes
items.summary: Presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged the Federal Government to take decisive action against those behind the killings and kidnappings across the country, saying the attackers are known and should be stopped. Obi made the call on Tuesday during a visit to an Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camp in Mangu Local […] Peter Obi urges FG to end killing
items.body: Presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged the Federal Government to take decisive action against those behind the killings and kidnappings across the country, saying the attackers are known and should be stopped. Obi made the call on Tuesday during a visit to an Internally Displaced Persons (IDP) camp in Mangu Local Government Area of Plateau State, where he sympathised with thousands of people forced to flee their communities due to insecurity. He said prayers were important in addressing the country’s security challenges but insisted that government action was necessary to end the violence. “I listen to somebody who says we need prayers. Yes, we need prayers. But the prayers can be solved by government. The people who are coming to kill people are not from the moon. We know them. The Nigerian government should be able to deal with it,” Obi said. The former Anambra State governor described the continued existence of IDP camps as unacceptable, saying displaced persons should be assisted to return safely to their homes. He said Nigeria could not truly be at peace while citizens remained in IDP camps, stressing that displaced persons should not be living there but should be able to return safely to their homes. Obi expressed concern over the scale of displacement in Plateau, noting that about 45,000 people from more than 20 communities had been forced out of their homes. He explained that his visit was not a campaign activity but a show of solidarity with victims of insecurity. “I came here today, not to campaign. I came to assure you that you are in our mind, we are thinking about you, and we are hoping that one day none of you will be here because you have gone back to your home,” he said. Obi also lamented the effect of insecurity on children’s education. According to him, the destruction of communities had disrupted learning for many young people. He praised the resilience of the displaced persons after seeing them sing and dance despite their hardships and assured them that they were not alone. Peter Obi urges FG to end killings, return IDPs to their homes

items.title: Police intensify manhunt for two armed robbery suspects in Delta
items.summary: The two suspects attacked a 48-year-old man in his residence with a locally-made gun on Friday at about 5:30 p.m., the police said. The post Police intensify manhunt for two armed robbery suspects in Delta appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .
items.body:
The Police Command in Delta State has intensified its manhunt for two armed robbery suspects in the state.

Bright Edafe, the police spokesperson in Delta, said in a statement on Tuesday in Warri that the suspects were among those terrorising Ekpan Community in Uvwie Local Government Area of the state.

He said the duo attacked a 48-year-old man in his residence with a locally-made gun on Friday at about 5:30 p.m.

Mr Edafe, a superintendent of police, said the incident was reported the same day at the Ekpan Division of the Nigeria Police.

The police spokesperson said the masked suspects broke into the victim’s house near Charlisco, on the NPA Express Road.

He said the victim courageously wrestled with the suspect holding the firearm, breaking the gun in the process.

Mr Edafe added that upon noticing this, the second suspect struck the victim on the forehead before both suspects fled, abandoning the broken firearm.

“Upon receipt of the report, the Divisional Police Officer, Ekpan Division, immediately deployed operatives to the scene, where the damaged locally-made firearm was recovered.

“The victim was referred to a hospital for treatment, while a manhunt for the fleeing suspects is in top gear,” he said.

Mr Edafe quoted the Commissioner of Police in the state, Samuel Erale, as commending the victim for his courage, and assured that the command would track and apprehend the suspects.

The police commissioner also solicited useful information from the public to assist the police in preventing crimes before they are committed in the state.

items.title: IGP, NBA president move to end police-lawyer clashes
items.summary: The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, and the President of the Nigerian Bar Association, NBA, Mrs Oyinkansola Badejo-Okusanya, SAN, have agreed to strengthen professional collaboration and communication to curb recurring clashes between lawyers and police officers and improve justice delivery. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, disclosed this in a statement […
items.body: The Inspector-General of Police, IGP Olatunji Rilwan Disu, and the President of the Nigerian Bar Association, NBA, Mrs Oyinkansola Badejo-Okusanya, SAN, have agreed to strengthen professional collaboration and communication to curb recurring clashes between lawyers and police officers and improve justice delivery. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Ani Iniedu, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday following the NBA President’s visit to the Force Headquarters, Abuja, where both institutions discussed ways to deepen cooperation within the justice system. Badejo-Okusanya called for closer engagement between the Police and the Bar, including specialised training for lawyers and stronger interaction between Police lawyers and members of the wider legal profession. She stressed that lawyers and police officers have complementary responsibilities in the justice system and urged both sides to end confrontations that could undermine public confidence in the administration of justice. The NBA President also highlighted a UNICEF-supported initiative on children’s access to justice, proposing that a police lawyer be available at every police station to provide legal support to children who come into contact with the juvenile justice system. Responding, Disu said the Police and legal profession must operate as partners in the pursuit of justice, noting that while lawyers protect citizens’ rights and the Police protect lives and property, both responsibilities ultimately converge in the justice system. He called for greater professionalism in handling encounters between police officers and lawyers, particularly in the recording and dissemination of such incidents on social media. The IGP also identified delays in criminal trials as an area requiring urgent collaboration, proposing a dedicated Nigeria Police Force/NBA communication mechanism to address professional concerns and resolve disputes before they escalate. Disu acknowledged that disagreements may arise between both professions but insisted that such differences must be managed with civility, professionalism and mutual respect. He assured the NBA leadership of his readiness to build a stronger partnership aimed at improving access to justice, protecting fundamental rights and strengthening Nigeria’s criminal justice system. IGP, NBA president move to end police-lawyer clashes

items.title: Drone strike near courthouse in North Kordofan kills 12
items.summary: A drone strike blamed on Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) killed 12 people and The post Drone strike near courthouse in North Kordofan kills 12 appeared first on Radio Tamazuj .
items.body: A drone strike blamed on Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) killed 12 people and wounded 20 others outside a courthouse in the army-held town of Um Rawaba in North Kordofan on Tuesday afternoon, army-aligned authorities and eyewitnesses told Radio Tamazuj. The strike was the latest in an escalating wave of drone attacks by the RSF and Sudanese army, which have been at war since April 2023. The drone struck an area outside the courthouse where residents had gathered to complete legal and administrative procedures, witnesses said. “The drone attack today targeted a courthouse in Um Rawaba and those killed are 12 and are all civilians, and many others have been wounded,” eyewitness Hamza Abdalla told Radio Tamazuj. The strikes sparked panic, prompting people to flee while others rushed to help the injured, the eyewitness said. Most of the wounded were taken to Um Rawaba Hospital for treatment, he added. Mohamed Salah, a spokesman for Sudan’s Emergency Lawyers Committee, a group of lawyers and human rights defenders, confirmed the reported toll of 12 dead and 20 wounded, including six lawyers and an employee of the judicial authority. “The attack targeted several areas, especially the courthouse, and those killed are 12 and wounded are 20 others,” Salah said. Salah said the attack occurred while legal professionals and court employees were carrying out their civilian duties. He described it as part of what he called a broader pattern of attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure. The lawyers’ spokesperson said attacks on civilian and legal facilities violate international humanitarian law and warned that such incidents could disrupt judicial institutions and limit civilians’ access to justice. Salah said the attack followed previous strikes on civilian and legal facilities, including an attack on the Garra al-Zawiya court in North Kordofan in August. The North Kordofan state government condemned the attack in a statement obtained by Radio Tamazuj, describing it as an attack on civilian institutions and judicial facilities. حكومة شمال كردفان تدين استهداف المليشيا مجمع المحاكم بأم روابة https://t.co/0FDrcW2cOz #سونا #السودان pic.twitter.com/IqbpWOjt8T — SUDAN News Agency (SUNA) (@SUNA_AGENCY) September 8, 2026 An RSF military official declined to comment when reached by Radio Tamazuj, saying only that Um Rawaba was hosting a graduation ceremony at the time for a group of army-affiliated fighters. Um Rawaba lies along a strategic route linking central and western Sudan and has remained under army control despite repeated attacks in the surrounding region. Sudan’s war has killed more than 200,000 people, according to aid workers, displaced millions and created the world’s largest displacement and hunger crises. In a video on his verified Facebook page, Fayose said Obi’s gentleman’s nature may cost him the […] We can’t take Presidency wit
items.body: Isaac Fayose, younger brother to former Ekiti State Governor, Ayodele Fayose, has expressed disappointment at the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, presidential candidate, Peter Obi, over the handling of the Benue State incident where suspected thugs attacked his convoy. In a video on his verified Facebook page, Fayose said Obi’s gentleman’s nature may cost him the Presidency. He criticised Obi for leaving Benue for Plateau after the incident without accomplishing his humanitarian visit to the Internally Displaced Persons, IDPs. According to him, to win the 2027 presidential elections requires a more aggressive and confrontational approach. “I am highly disappointed in Mr Peter Obi today. Why will he leave Benue State for Plateau State without accomplishing his mission? My leader, you are a Nigerian; you have the right to travel anywhere. “How are we going to take the government from Tinubu and the ruling All Progressives Congress, APC? “If they bring thugs, we bring our own thugs. Thugs for thugs, fire for fire, trouble for trouble. If we are playing this gentleman’s game, we’re going to lose our election. “I’m very sad that you left Benue. Other state governors will want to do it to you because they know you are gentle” he lamented. Watch video: We can’t take Presidency with your gentleman nature -Isaac Fayose to Peter Obi

items.title: Gunshots as police, traffic officials clash in Edo
items.summary: There was pandemonium at Third Junction, Benin City, Edo state, on Tuesday as officers of the Intelligence Response Team (IRT) reportedly engaged in physical confrontation [...]
items.body:
There was pandemonium at Third Junction, Benin City, Edo state, on Tuesday as officers of the Intelligence Response Team (IRT) reportedly engaged in physical confrontation with personnel of the Edo State Traffic Management Agency (EDSTMA), leaving at least one traffic official injured.

The incident, which occurred at first junction by Sokponba road at about 3:00p.m., reportedly triggered gunshots, forcing motorists, pedestrians, traders and other members of the public in the busy area to scamper for safety

A witness, who identified himself as Ezekiel Obi, said members of the public were forced to run in different directions in an attempt to avoid being caught in the confrontation, amid fears that stray bullets could hit innocent persons.

“The situation was frightening, particularly because of the large number of people around the junction when the incident occurred,” Obi stated.

According to him, the sudden development created confusion among motorists and pedestrians, many of whom hurried away from the scene for fear of being caught in the line of fire.

The immediate cause of the confrontation between the police officers and EDSTMA officials could not be independently established as of press time.

However, Blueprint gathered that an argument between personnel of the two agencies reportedly escalated into a physical confrontation before firearms were allegedly discharged.

The incident reportedly disrupted normal activities around the junction for some time, with motorists and pedestrians keeping away from the immediate vicinity of the confrontation.

A resident, who simply identified himself as Obaze, expressed concern over what he described as the increasingly aggressive approach allegedly adopted by some personnel of specialised police units while carrying out their duties.

Obaze alleged that similar incidents involving what he described as a “commando-style” approach had occurred in the past, urging the relevant authorities to ensure that law enforcement operations did not expose members of the public to unnecessary danger.

He emphasised that while security personnel had a responsibility to maintain law and order, their operations should also take into consideration the safety of innocent residents, motorists and other road users.

The Public Relations Officer of Edo State police Command, Eno Ikoedem was yet to comment on the development as of the time of filing this report.

items.title: Troops foil attacks, rescue kidnap victims in Zamfara
items.summary: Troops of the Joint Task Force (North West), Operation FANSAN YAMMA, have rescued 12 civilians during separate operations in Kaura Namoda and Tsafe local government areas of Zamfara State. The operations were conducted as part of efforts to disrupt terrorist activities and protect civilians across the state. In Kaura Namoda, troops responded to a distress […]
items.body: Troops of the Joint Task Force (North West), Operation FANSAN YAMMA, have rescued 12 civilians during separate operations in Kaura Namoda and Tsafe local government areas of Zamfara State. The operations were conducted as part of efforts to disrupt terrorist activities and protect civilians across the state. In Kaura Namoda, troops responded to a distress call following the infiltration of terrorists into a residence at Tsohon Tasha. The troops engaged the terrorists in a gun battle, forcing them to abandon six abducted civilians and flee across a nearby river. NSCIA alleges religious bias in El-Rufai’s incarceration Military rulers treated Nigeria’s oil wealth as ‘spoils of war’ — Prof. Aluko The rescued victims were subsequently evacuated and reunited with their families, according to a statement by the Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force (North West), Operation FANSAN YAMMA, Lieutenant Colonel Aliyu Danja. In a separate operation in Tsafe LGA, troops monitoring activities along the Main Supply Route observed terrorists attempting to intercept a Sharon vehicle at Kwanoni Village. The troops swiftly mobilised to the area and engaged the terrorists, forcing them to abandon the operation and retreat into the adjoining bush and the intervention also led to the rescue of six civilians. Danja said the operations demonstrated the troops’ commitment to protecting lives and property while disrupting terrorist activities and denying the criminals freedom of action within the Joint Operations Area. He urged members of the public to continue providing security agencies with relevant information to support ongoing efforts to eliminate terrorist elements from the area.

items.title: Vigilante killed as bandits attack Kano village
items.summary: Bandits invaded Dakwara village in Gwarzo Local Government Area of Kano State in the early hours of Tuesday, killing a vigilante and abducting a resident. The village head, Usman Ibrahim, told Daily Trust that the attackers stormed the community around 4:00 a.m., shooting sporadically and demanding motorcycles. “They killed Abdulmuminu Bichila, a vigilante who tried […]
items.body: Bandits invaded Dakwara village in Gwarzo Local Government Area of Kano State in the early hours of Tuesday, killing a vigilante and abducting a resident. The village head, Usman Ibrahim, told Daily Trust that the attackers stormed the community around 4:00 a.m., shooting sporadically and demanding motorcycles. “They killed Abdulmuminu Bichila, a vigilante who tried to rescue a boy they had seized. The boy managed to escape, but the vigilante was shot dead,” he said. According to him, the gunmen first robbed a man of his motorcycle before entering Dakwara. NSCIA alleges religious bias in El-Rufai’s incarceration Military rulers treated Nigeria’s oil wealth as ‘spoils of war’ — Prof. Aluko They later moved to Kadanyar Sallau village where they seized two more motorcycles and fled. Ibrahim added that the bandits also abducted a man from Getso town in Gwarzo, though he was not taken through Dakwara. Residents later received reports that the abducted man was rescued after a clash between security forces and the bandits in Kafur Local Government Area of Katsina State, where some of the attackers were killed and stolen motorcycles recovered. The village head said the attackers came from the eastern axis of Gwarzo towards Kutama, which borders Katsina. “Most of them were Fulani from Katsina, not Kano. This was the first time they attacked our town, though they had previously struck other parts of Gwarzo like Lakwaya, Rugoji, Gangara and Kutama,” he explained. He noted that Dakwara lies only six kilometres from Gwarzo town and about the same distance from Kutama, making the community vulnerable to cross border incursions. When contacted, the Public Relations Officer of 3rd Brigade of Nigerian Army in Kano, Capt Zubairu Babatunde, said they were not aware of the attack. The incident adds to a series of bandit attacks in Kano LGAs especially those sharing borders with Katsina and Kaduna states, with residents calling for stronger security presence to protect border communities.

items.title: 2027: Security agencies strategise against election violence in Kogi
items.summary: Security agencies and electoral stakeholders in Kogi State have begun preparations for the 2027 general election, with officials calling for collaboration, compliance with electoral laws, and peaceful political campaigns. The post 2027: Security agencies strategise against election violence in Kogi appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .
items.body:
Security agencies and other stakeholders in Kogi State have begun preparations for the 2027 general election, with a focus on preventing violence and other threats that could undermine the electoral process.

The stakeholders met in Lokoja under the Inter-Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES) to review emerging security threats and strengthen coordination ahead of the elections.

The Kogi Resident Electoral Commissioner, Shehu Wahab, who spoke at the meeting, said the committee had a responsibility to deploy its experience and resources to ensure voters could exercise their franchise peacefully.

He said the meeting provided an opportunity for security agencies to review security concerns and determine measures required to safeguard the electoral process.

The meeting, which lasted about two hours, was held behind closed doors as members reviewed security concerns and other issues surrounding the 2027 elections.

The Kogi State Commissioner of Police, Naziru Kankarofi, subsequently urged political actors to comply with electoral laws and avoid hate speech, incitement and other actions capable of disrupting public peace.

He also called for responsible political communication and peaceful campaigns ahead of the elections.

Mr Wahab said the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) was putting measures in place to support the work of ICCES and strengthen efforts towards a peaceful and credible election in the state.

He acknowledged that Kogi, like other states in Nigeria, has areas facing security challenges, adding that the security committee was designed to address such concerns through collaboration among relevant agencies.

The development comes a day after PREMIUM TIMES reported that Governor Ahmed Ododo banned night arrests and urged traditional rulers to work toward peaceful, violence-free elections.

Mr Ododo, while addressing first-class traditional rulers at the Government House in Lokoja on Monday, directed security agencies not to invade homes or make arrests at night.

He also urged the monarchs to discourage political thuggery, intimidation and violence, and to ensure that political campaigns are issue-based rather than driven by religion or ethnicity.

The governor’s directive and the latest security meeting come as Kogi begins early preparations for the 2027 electoral process, with stakeholders stressing the need for security agencies, political actors and communities to work together to prevent violence.

items.title: CBN Elevates Terrorism Financing Supervision As Current Priority
items.summary: According to the CBN, the measures will be implemented in accordance with existing legal and regulatory requirements. The post CBN Elevates Terrorism Financing Supervision As Current Priority appeared first on Channels Television .
items.body: The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has intensified its supervisory focus on terrorism financing, making it a current priority in its efforts to prevent the country’s financial system from being exploited by illicit actors. The apex bank disclosed this in a statement signed by its Acting Director, Corporate Communications and Investor Relations Department, Hakama Sidi-Ali. Under the heightened supervisory focus, the CBN said it would pay particular attention to terrorism financing risk management, transaction monitoring, implementation of targeted financial sanctions and the reporting of suspicious transactions linked to terrorism financing. The bank said it would continue to deploy a risk-based supervisory approach, including on-site and off-site engagements, to strengthen anti-money laundering, counter-financing of terrorism and counter-proliferation financing (AML/CFT/CPF) controls across the financial sector. According to the CBN, the measures will be implemented in accordance with existing legal and regulatory requirements. The apex bank said the move also supports Nigeria’s domestic and international cooperation on counter-terrorism financing, counter-proliferation financing and broader efforts to strengthen financial integrity and protect the financial system. “Further supervisory engagement will be undertaken as appropriate,” the CBN added. The bank said the initiative underscores its ongoing commitment to safeguarding the Nigerian financial system against illicit activities while supporting efforts to strengthen financial integrity at both domestic and international levels. The post CBN Elevates Terrorism Financing Supervision As Current Priority appeared first on Channels Television .

items.title: Abiodun says 100,000 Ogun women empowered to fight poverty, strengthen families
items.summary: Abiodun said about 100,000 women across the state have benefited from the World Bank-supported Nigeria for Women Programme (NFWP), describing women’s economic empowerment as a strategic tool for fighting poverty and strengthening families and communities The post Abiodun says 100,000 Ogun women empowered to fight poverty, strengthen families appeared first on Premium Times Nigeria .
items.body:
L-R: United Nations Deputy Secretary-General, Ms Amina Mohammed, receiving a plaque of honour from the Ogun State Governor, Prince Dapo Abiodun, during her visit to the State on Tuesday.

Ogun State Governor Prince Dapo Abiodun has disclosed that about 100,000 women across the state have benefited from the World Bank-supported Nigeria for Women Programme (NFWP), describing women’s economic empowerment as a strategic tool for fighting poverty and strengthening families and communities.

Abiodun made the disclosure on Monday when he received the United Nations Deputy Secretary-General, Ms Amina Mohammed, who joined him in interacting with beneficiaries of the programme at the Governor’s Office, Oke-Mosan, Abeokuta.

The governor said his administration deliberately embraced and took ownership of the programme because it provided an opportunity to reach women at the grassroots who might otherwise remain outside conventional structures of political and economic empowerment.

According to him, empowering women should go beyond appointing them to political offices to providing them with the resources, skills and opportunities required to build sustainable livelihoods, support their families and live with dignity.

“When the World Bank shared with us the Nigeria for Women Project, we did not only key into it; we took ownership of it.

“We saw in that programme the opportunity to empower women because not all women are able to contest elections or be appointed Commissioners or occupy political offices. We saw the opportunity to touch the lives of these women, empower them to support their households and themselves, and give them a sense of dignity,” he said.

Abiodun said the programme’s impact had reinforced his administration’s conviction that investing in women was an investment in the wider economy and the future of families. He noted that economically empowered women were better positioned to provide for their households and contribute to community development.

He said Ogun’s implementation of the programme had attracted delegations from more than 25 states seeking to study the state’s model, adding that political commitment remained critical to replicating its success.

The governor expressed the hope that the initiative would be expanded across the country so that more women could benefit from the intervention.

“It is my prayer that this deepens across the length and breadth of the 36 states and the FCT. I am filled with so much joy today that you are here and that you can see first-hand what we have been able to do with women empowerment,” Abiodun said.

The UN deputy secretary-general commended the governor for providing seed funding for the programme and, more importantly, for believing in the capacity of women to grow their businesses and transform their communities.

Mohammed praised the beneficiaries for demonstrating resilience, creativity and enterprise, saying their progress showed what could be achieved when women were given the right support and opportunities.

“You have shown that you started small and you are growing, and what we want is for every woman in Ogun State who can benefit to have that benefit,” she said.

The UN official said she would take the Ogun experience back to her home state and share it as an example of what could be achieved through deliberate investment in women.

“I will take this initiative back to my state so that everyone will know that a seed was sown in Ogun State for the women of Nigeria, and that seed is growing. A country is as strong as its women,” Mohammed added.

The State Coordinator of the Nigeria for Women Programme, Mrs. Bola Fadairo, disclosed that Ogun was among the first six pilot states when the programme was launched in 2020.

She said the state had exceeded its target by 105 percent, with 8,759 Women Affinity Groups comprising 247,273 women established across the 20 local government areas.

Fadairo added that beneficiaries had received training in financial management, record-keeping, gender awareness, life skills and other areas designed to equip them with the knowledge and skills required to build sustainable livelihoods.

She said the scale of participation and the impact recorded across the state underscored Ogun’s commitment to creating sustainable opportunities for women to strengthen their livelihoods, improve household incomes and contribute meaningfully to the development of their communities.

items.title: BCLCC : Le ministre Mahamadou Sana inaugure un studio dédié à la lutte contre les fakes news et à la sensibilisation à la cybercriminalité
items.summary: Le Ministre de la Sécurité, le Camarade Mahamadou SANA, a procédé, dans l’après-midi de ce mardi 8 septembre 2026, à l’inauguration du studio multimédia de la Brigade Centrale de Lutte contre la Cybercriminalité (BCLCC). Cette infrastructure moderne est destinée à renforcer la communication préventive et la sensibilisation des populations face aux défis croissants du numérique. … The post BCLCC :
items.body:
Le Ministre de la Sécurité, le Camarade Mahamadou SANA, a procédé, dans l’après-midi de ce mardi 8 septembre 2026, à l’inauguration du studio multimédia de la Brigade Centrale de Lutte contre la Cybercriminalité (BCLCC). Cette infrastructure moderne est destinée à renforcer la communication préventive et la sensibilisation des populations face aux défis croissants du numérique.

Doté d’équipements audiovisuels de dernière génération, ce studio servira à produire des capsules dédiées à la déconstruction des fausses informations (fake news), à la sensibilisation à la cybersécurité et à la vulgarisation de diverses thématiques en lien avec la sécurité.

À travers cet investissement, le Ministère de la Sécurité se dote d’un outil stratégique pour promouvoir une information fiable, développer une culture de cybersécurité et renforcer la résilience des citoyens face aux menaces numériques.

Le studio contribuera également à l’éducation des populations aux enjeux du numérique, à la prévention des risques liés à l’utilisation des technologies de l’information et de la communication, ainsi qu’à la promotion des bonnes pratiques en ligne.

Cette réalisation traduit la volonté du Gouvernement, sous l’impulsion du Camarade Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim TRAORE, de faire de la communication de proximité et de la prévention des risques numériques un levier majeur de la stratégie nationale de sécurité.

À travers des contenus pédagogiques, accessibles et adaptés aux réalités des citoyens, la BCLCC entend renforcer la vigilance collective et accompagner les populations dans une utilisation responsable et sécurisée des outils numériques.

items.title: Sudan Is Not Short of Warnings. It Is Short of Funding.
items.summary: Sudan does not lack global attention in the abstract sense. In the space of a single week in September 2026, the UN's human rights chief renewed calls to end a war now in its fourth year, the Security Council debated another arms-embargo extension, and Médecins Sans Frontières issued perhaps its bluntest warning yet: the country's healthcare system is on the brink of total collapse. What Sudan act
items.body:
Displaced Somali women hold their severely malnourished babies in a stabilization centre for children suffering severe accute malnutrition in Kismayo, Somalia on April 22. Today across Africa, women and girls remain caught in a confluence of armed conflict, forced displacement, food insecurity, climate shock and systemic poverty, says the writer.

The scale is difficult to overstate. Since fighting erupted between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces in April 2023, roughly 14 million people have been displaced, including some 7.1 million internally and 4.4 million who crossed into Chad, Egypt, South Sudan and beyond , figures that make Sudan the world's largest displacement crisis, ahead of Syria and Ukraine at their respective peaks. UN Human Rights Chief Volker Türk this week pointed specifically to strikes on "markets, hospitals and fuel stations," citing a drone attack on a kindergarten and hospital in South Kordofan that killed 114 people, including 60 children, and a separate assault on a teaching hospital that killed at least 70. The UN's $2.87 billion humanitarian response plan for Sudan is only 41% funded, even as needs keep climbing.

MSF's warning, delivered directly to world leaders gathered at the UN General Assembly, is not speculative, it is describing a system unravelling month by month. Roughly 37% of Sudan's health facilities are now out of service. In central Darfur, MSF-supported facilities saw patient admissions rise 22.5% between January and April 2026 compared with the same period a year earlier, even as 45 healthcare centres in the same region lost their funding in May alone. In Tawila, North Darfur, MSF runs the only 200-bed hospital serving up to 600,000 displaced people and remains the sole organisation capable of running large-scale epidemic control, at precisely the moment malaria and malnutrition cases are climbing ahead of the rainy season's peak.

The charity is explicit about the cause: the closure of USAID last year, whose Sudan grants expired in June, combined with a 35.8% year-on-year drop in global aid funding, has pushed patients who once had other options onto a shrinking number of remaining clinics, including MSF's own, which the organisation notes are privately funded and now absorbing pressure meant for a much larger system. Attacks on healthcare workers compound the collapse: Sudan alone accounted for 82% of all recorded global deaths from attacks on medical facilities in 2025.

Sudan's trajectory echoes two precedents the international community would rather not repeat. Yemen's health system suffered an almost identical funding-driven unravelling after 2018, when donor fatigue and geopolitical distraction let cholera and malnutrition metastasise inside hospitals that had simply run out of money to operate, a slow collapse driven less by any single battle than by the world's attention moving elsewhere. Syria offers the harder parallel: a Security Council repeatedly unable to act decisively because of great-power vetoes, allowing a conflict to grind on for over a decade while humanitarian carve-outs became routine rather than exceptional. Sudan now shows the same pattern , Russia has already signalled resistance to expanding the Darfur arms embargo to cover the whole country, exactly the kind of council paralysis that let Syria's war outlast three US presidencies.

What distinguishes Sudan's crisis from a purely military failure is how avoidable the healthcare collapse specifically is. This is not a system undone by an impossible medical challenge; it is one being starved by a funding shortfall that governments could close if they chose to. MSF's ask is narrow and specific, sustained, flexible funding to keep existing facilities open rather than a grand diplomatic breakthrough , precisely because the healthcare piece of this crisis is one of the few parts still within reach of a fix that does not depend on ending the war first. Ceasefire calls matter, and Secretary-General António Guterres is right to keep repeating his. But if Sudan's hospitals close before a ceasefire ever arrives, the international community will have managed to lose the argument it was never actually contesting: keeping people alive while the diplomats keep talking.

items.title: RSF-aligned gov’t rejects UN fact-finding report as biased
items.summary: The paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) aligned government, the Sudan Founding Alliance (Tasees) has rejected... The post RSF-aligned gov’t rejects UN fact-finding report as biased appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .
items.body: The paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) aligned government, the Sudan Founding Alliance (Tasees) has rejected a report by the UN fact-finding mission on Sudan, accusing it of bias and ignoring alleged crimes committed by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF). The alliance said it remains ready to cooperate with international human rights mechanisms and reaffirmed its commitment to international human rights and international criminal law. The report , presented to the Human Rights Council on Monday, cited a cross-border network involving the UAE, Chad, Libya and Puntland that allegedly supports the RSF with weapons. It also referred to crimes committed in El Fasher. Tasees spokesperson Ahmed Tagad Lisan, said in a statement seen by Radio Dabanga that the report contained “fundamental systematic defects” that undermine its conclusions and legal credibility. He criticised the mission’s reliance on remote testimonies and interviews conducted away from the locations of alleged violations, saying investigators had failed to conduct direct field inspections. Tasees accuses report of ignoring SAF violations Tasees accused the report of systematically overlooking alleged violations by the SAF and allied militias, including the alleged use of internationally banned chemical weapons . Tagad Lisan said the report failed to provide a balanced assessment of responsibility. He pointed to alleged massacres in El Gezira state, Sennar, Suki, Singa and El Dinder, as well as the Haj Yousif, Mayo, El Salih and El Halfaya neighbourhoods of the capital following the SAF’s entry. He accused SAF forces and allied militias of carrying out “clean-up operations” involving the execution of hundreds of civilians, destruction of homes and farms, forced displacement and looting. Tasees said the omission of these alleged crimes raised questions about the report’s neutrality. Tasees accuses mission of bias Tasees also accused the report of presenting a one-sided account of foreign involvement in the war. It said the report highlighted alleged support for its forces from Chad, south-eastern Libya, Puntland, the UAE and Colombia, while failing to mention countries it said support the SAF, including Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Türkiye, Qatar, Iran, Algeria and Eritrea. Tasees also criticised the report for mentioning Colombian recruits fighting alongside its forces while allegedly omitting references to Eritrean military bases, Ethiopian forces, Egyptian forces and other foreign elements fighting alongside the SAF and allied militias. Tasees called for the report’s conclusions to be reviewed and for a direct field investigation under international supervision covering all conflict zones. It also called for investigators to hear from all parties and examine documented violations committed by all sides. Share article The post RSF-aligned gov’t rejects UN fact-finding report as biased appeared first on Dabanga Radio TV Online .

items.title: Al-Burhan Meets ICGLR Delegation
items.summary: [SNA] President of Transitional Sovereignty Council (TSC) and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, General Abdel-Fattah Al-Burhan, met on Sunday with a delegation from the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR), headed by the organization's Secretary-General, Joël Kianda.
items.body:
President of Transitional Sovereignty Council (TSC) and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, General Abdel-Fattah Al-Burhan, met on Sunday with a delegation from the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR), headed by the organization's Secretary-General, Joël Kianda.

The meeting was attended by the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Ambassador Mohi-Eddin Salem.

In a press statement, the ICGLR Secretary-General said the organization regarded Sudan as an important and pivotal country in Africa, describing the meeting with the TSC President as fruitful and constructive, particularly in light of Sudan's contribution to advancing African issues.

He stressed that Sudan believed in the need to resolve African problems within the African framework, away from international interference.

Kianda said the meeting also discussed a number of issues of mutual interest, foremost among them the importance of sustaining security and stability in the Great Lakes region and the wider region.

He said the ICGLR had confidence that the region was in safe hands and that Sudan was on the right path, reaffirming the organization's support for Sudan during the current critical phase until peace and stability are achieved throughout the country.

items.title: Sudan: Finance Minister - Armed Forces Constitutional Institution Responsible for Protecting Sudan - Rejects Expansion of Arms Embargo
items.summary: [SNA] Chairman of the Sudanese Justice and Equality Movement (JEM) and Minister of Finance, Dr. Gebreil Ibrahim Mohamed, affirmed that the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) are the national institution constitutionally mandated to protect the country and defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity, announcing JEM's rejection of proposals to expand the arms embargo imposed on Darfur to cover all of
items.body:
Chairman of the Sudanese Justice and Equality Movement (JEM) and Minister of Finance, Dr. Gebreil Ibrahim Mohamed, affirmed that the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) are the national institution constitutionally mandated to protect the country and defend its sovereignty and territorial integrity, announcing JEM's rejection of proposals to expand the arms embargo imposed on Darfur to cover all of Sudan.

In a post on his official Facebook page following a meeting in Khartoum on Sunday with the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy to Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, Dr. Gebreil said such a measure would undermine national sovereignty and restrict the Armed Forces' ability to fulfill their constitutional duty to protect the country.

The meeting discussed developments in Sudan, particularly the humanitarian situation and violations against civilians by the rebel Rapid Support Forces (RSF) militia.

Dr. Gebreil stressed the importance of the international community playing a supportive role in safeguarding Sudan's sovereignty, territorial integrity and the legitimacy of its national institutions.

He also reviewed prospects for the political process and pathways toward peace, stressing the importance of pursuing two complementary tracks simultaneously: the security track based on the Jeddah Declaration, and the political track through an inclusive Sudanese dialogue that excludes no one.

He called on the United Nations to welcome and support the Sudanese dialogue initiative and to work with Sudanese stakeholders to develop it into an inclusive, Sudanese-owned political process that would bring an end to the war and lay the foundations for sustainable peace and a stable state.

Dr. Gebreil reaffirmed the movement's commitment to integrating its forces into the Sudanese Armed Forces, stressing the importance of integrating all armed forces into a unified national army.

items.title: TSC President Meets UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy to Sudan
items.summary: [SNA] President of the Transitional Sovereignty Council (TSC) and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, General Abdel-Fattah Al-Burhan, met on Sunday at his office in the Republican Palace with the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy to Sudan, Pekka Haavisto.
items.body:
President of the Transitional Sovereignty Council (TSC) and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, General Abdel-Fattah Al-Burhan, met on Sunday at his office in the Republican Palace with the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy to Sudan, Pekka Haavisto.

The meeting discussed the overall situation in Sudan, efforts to strengthen security and stability, and the achievement of comprehensive peace in the country.

In a press statement, Haavisto said: "I conveyed important messages concerning de-escalation and the protection of civilians. We also look forward to continuing our meetings with a view to achieving the exchange of prisoners and civilian detainees, in close cooperation with the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC)."

Haavisto stressed that dialogue was the path to achieving sustainable peace and reaching a comprehensive ceasefire. He expressed his readiness to cooperate and engage in close dialogue with all Sudanese parties and stakeholders, and to work with partners in the Quintet to advance the political process and ensure that it is inclusive, comprehensive and responsive to the aspirations of the Sudanese people.

He also stressed the importance of holding unified examinations across the country, describing the issue as a major concern for the international community. The United Nations, he said, was working closely with UNICEF to safeguard children's fundamental right to sit for accredited examinations across Sudan.

Haavisto concluded his remarks by praising reconstruction efforts, saying: "I can see and observe many construction and reconstruction works bringing life back to normal in this city."

items.title: Nigeria: Clashes Claim 2 Lives in Bauchi
items.summary: [Daily Trust] The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested seven suspects in connection with the criminal conspiracy, inciting disturbance and culpable homicide that occurred in Dass Local Government Area on 4th September, 2026.
items.body:
The Bauchi State Police Command has arrested seven suspects in connection with the criminal conspiracy, inciting disturbance and culpable homicide that occurred in Dass Local Government Area on 4th September, 2026.

The command's Public Relations Officer, SP Nafiu Habib, who disclosed this in a statement, said preliminary investigation revealed that on the said date at about 1800hrs, one Ibrahim El-Safwan aka Jabala'i of Bayan Fada area, Dass, criminally conspired with his accomplices, intercepted and brutally attacked one Abdulrahman Nuru, 29-years-old, a tricycle rider of Bundot area, Dass, stabbing him with cutlasses on various parts of his body at Tudun Wus area, Dass.

Habib said that a team of policemen attached to Dass Division swiftly mobilised to the scene.

"On arrival, it was discovered that personnel of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, whose headquarters is close to the scene, had already taken custody of the tricycle and one suspect.

"The victim was immediately rushed to General Hospital, Dass, where he was subsequently confirmed dead by a medical doctor," he said.

Habib explained that the incident sparked tension in the area, as youths from Bundot area mobilised in large numbers, armed with cutlasses and other dangerous weapons, and stormed the Bayan Fada area for reprisal.

"This led to a violent confrontation between the two groups at an open space near Dass' Central Motor Park, during which another victim, Mukhtar Jibrin, 38 years old, of Bayan Fada area, was stabbed.

"Mukhtar was rushed to General Hospital, Dass, and later referred to the Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital, Bauchi, where he was also confirmed dead," he said.

He, however, noted that detectives swung into action, doused the tension, restored normalcy, and arrested the following suspects in connection with the ugly incident: Umar Abubakar 20-years-old of Bayan Fada area (principal suspect), Blus Garba 19-years-old Bundot area, Adamu Muhammad 17-years-old of Bundot area, Hussaini Danjuma 17-years-old of Bundot area, Hassan Danjuma 17-years-old of Bundot area, Shuaibu Sani 17-years-old of Bundot area, and Aliyu Abdullahi 18-years-old of Bundot area.

Habib further disclosed that relentless efforts are in top gear to apprehend other accomplices now at large.

items.title: Kaduna: Stolen newborn found, suspect arrested
items.summary: A newborn stolen from a house in Sabon Gari New Extension, Kaduna South Local Government Area of Kaduna State, has been recovered in Unguwar Ma’azu area. The baby’s mother, Amina, said she was alerted on Monday evening that a woman in the area was claiming to have given birth, but residents became suspicious after the […]
items.body: A newborn stolen from a house in Sabon Gari New Extension, Kaduna South Local Government Area of Kaduna State, has been recovered in Unguwar Ma’azu area. The baby’s mother, Amina, said she was alerted on Monday evening that a woman in the area was claiming to have given birth, but residents became suspicious after the baby was seen crying and the woman could not breastfeed him. She said her elder sister’s daughter rushed to her house around Maghrib prayer and asked her to go and identify the baby. “When we got to the house, I entered the compound thinking that we were going there to congratulate the woman on her delivery. As soon as I entered, I saw the woman before I saw the baby, and I immediately recognised her as the same woman who came to my house and took my baby,” Amina said. Convoy Blockade: Call Governors to Order, Obi Tells IGP, DSS DG 30-year-old Man Shoots security Operative in Edo According to her, residents restrained her from confronting the woman while the police were contacted. “We went to the police station, where my baby was handed back to me. I am grateful and I thank everyone who prayed for me and helped in finding my baby,” she said. A resident, Malam Garba, who helped in locating the baby, said residents initially believed the woman had delivered three days earlier. He said the woman first claimed that her baby was in hospital before later saying the baby had died. “But when she was seen with a newborn baby, people became suspicious,” he said. He added that was why they looked for the woman whose baby had been reported stolen and asked her to come and check whether the baby was hers The incident occurred on Sunday when the suspect allegedly visited the family’s home and introduced herself as a distant relative of the baby’s father. The Kaduna State Police Command spokesman, DSP Mansir Hassan, confirmed the recovery of the baby, saying the suspect was undergoing interrogation as investigation continued.
